objective: Close the false-completion class at its source in IRIS Core rather than at one caller. packages/kernel/src/operating-decision-engine.ts line 66 short-circuits to report-terminal on a caller-supplied objective.terminal field, and no code in Core verifies that claim; the sibling task gateway-status-shortcut-false-completion explicitly excludes this file, so no record currently covers it. Core therefore delegates the determination of completion to an untrusted caller, which is how Certification Test One reported state completed for seven requirements it never addressed. Establish and enforce the invariant that IRIS Core never emits terminal state completed on the strength of an unverified caller assertion. Core-derived terminal outcomes, such as the unsupported result at line 105 that draws its evidence from the capability snapshot, remain legitimate and must be preserved. The producer must choose and state an exact design satisfying the invariant, survey every terminal emission site in Core, and record the chosen design and its rationale for independent review.

completion_exclusions: No change to the seven certification tests, their pass conditions, or the recorded Test One failure
No change to the canonical operating contract digest, its five decision outcomes, or protected-effect boundaries
No change to scripts/local-gateway.mjs or to the scope of the sibling task gateway-status-shortcut-false-completion
No weakening of fail-closed behavior, approval consumption, protected-path enforcement, or secret filtering
No Phase 0 graduation execution, approval, or completion claim
permitted_actions: Survey and report every site in IRIS Core that can emit a report-terminal decision, distinguishing Core-derived outcomes from caller-asserted ones

Choose and implement one exact design that satisfies the invariant, and state the choice and rationale in the specification; candidate designs include removing caller-supplied terminal entirely so Core derives every terminal outcome, restricting caller assertions to non-success states so completed can never be asserted, or requiring per-requirement evidence that Core verifies against the objective's stated requirements before accepting a completed claim
Extend the objective contract with an explicit stated-requirements representation if the chosen design needs Core to verify requirement coverage

Amend tests/operating-decision-engine.test.ts line 160, which currently pins the defective behavior by asserting that a caller-supplied terminal completed claim is reported verbatim; this amendment removes an assertion of the defect and is not test weakening, and the producer must justify it explicitly in the handoff
Make the minimum conforming updates to the other listed test files where they construct caller-asserted terminal objectives, reporting each amended test and its justification

Add regression tests covering at minimum: an unverified caller-asserted completed claim is rejected or cannot be expressed; a Core-derived unsupported outcome still reports correctly with snapshot evidence; and a structured objective with unaddressed requirements never yields terminal completed
prohibited_actions: Delete, skip, or loosen any existing test, guard, or fail-closed path to make the repair pass, other than the explicitly authorized amendments to tests that assert the defect
Change the canonical operating contract digest, the five decision outcomes, or the protected-effect set
Modify the certification program, the recorded Test One failure evidence, or any historical result
Repair the Command Center gateway or otherwise absorb the sibling task's scope
Claim this repair certifies Test One; it only removes one precondition for a fresh attempt from a new exact proposal
Force-push, rewrite history, bypass branch protection, administer repositories, or use broad staging
